supersession.reason: Hosted run 31796070637 retained all 1320 rows, each a setup failure before application traffic, because gateway and source-policy routes were installed before link activation and gateway/onlink semantics were omitted in implementation.

v3_smoke_diagnostic.reason: V3 smoke isolated R8 abrupt move timeout and TCP candidate receive without response while GARP passed. All smoke runs are diagnostic only with no result observations.

hypothesis: Under identical isolated-lab notice, trust, and load, Q1 reports R8 mobility, TCP reconnect, and GARP VIP movement without post-hoc tuning.

topology.network: IPv4-only isolated Linux namespaces on one host. Base namespace names are r8q1-client, r8q1-server, and r8q1-router; an operational random suffix is permitted only after each base name.
topology.links_and_addresses: client/router veth is 10.88.0.2/24 on client and 10.88.0.1/24 on router. Router server-side bridge is 10.88.1.1/24. Server old and candidate interfaces are separate veths with 10.88.1.2/24 and 10.88.1.3/24 respectively. VIP is 10.88.1.100/32.
topology.fixed_mac_addresses: While down, assign router bridge 02:00:00:00:01:01, old server interface 02:00:00:00:01:02, and candidate server interface 02:00:00:00:01:03.
topology.routing: Client has a static default route via 10.88.0.1. Server main route to 10.88.0.0/24 via 10.88.1.1 dev old is unchanged. Source 10.88.1.2/32 uses table 101, which first installs 10.88.1.0/24 dev old scope link, then 10.88.0.0/24 via 10.88.1.1 dev old. Source 10.88.1.3/32 uses table 102; temporarily bring candidate up solely to first install 10.88.1.0/24 dev candidate scope link and then 10.88.0.0/24 via 10.88.1.1 dev candidate onlink. VIP source uses table 103, which initially first installs 10.88.1.0/24 dev old scope link, then 10.88.0.0/24 via 10.88.1.1 dev old. These rules make bound TCP and R8 carriers use their actual interface while both are up. IPv4 forwarding is enabled only inside r8q1-router; no namespace has an outside route; no dynamic routing is permitted.
setup_order: assign fixed MAC addresses while down
bring router links and bridge up
temporarily bring candidate server link up solely for table 102 static connected and remote route installation
install permanent static neighbors identically for all mechanisms and arms
explicitly bring candidate server link down before pre-trial counters and clock
topology.setup_constraints: Temporary candidate activation is solely for static table 102 route installation; no traffic, neighbor flush, or dynamic discovery is permitted during setup. Candidate is administratively down for the initial trial state.
topology.server_strong_host_sysctls: Before trials, only in the isolated server namespace, set IPv4 rp_filter=0 and arp_ignore=1, arp_announce=2 for all, default, old, and candidate interfaces. This makes source-policy routes govern the multihomed return path and prevents the old interface from answering ARP for candidate or VIP; it is not public-network guidance.
topology.static_neighbors: Before the clock, install permanent static neighbors identically for every mechanism and arm: router bridge maps 10.88.1.2 to 02:00:00:00:01:02 and 10.88.1.3 to 02:00:00:00:01:03; each old and candidate server interface maps gateway 10.88.1.1 to 02:00:00:00:01:01. Do not install a static VIP neighbor: GARP remains measured. No neighbor flush or dynamic discovery is permitted; raw MACs and commands remain absent from evidence, which records only command hashes.
topology.dns: disabled; every endpoint is a numeric IPv4 address
topology.privileges: runner MUST start as root and retain CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_NET_RAW; missing privilege is setup failure and the run fails, never skips
topology.evidence_counts: interface_count is exactly 10 including three loopbacks; non_loopback_interface_count is exactly 7; veth_pair_count is exactly 3.
topology.teardown: teardown of owned namespaces removes their source-policy rules and routes.

traffic.payload: exactly 64 bytes: big-endian u64 sequence number followed by 56 zero bytes
traffic.rate: 100 Hz exactly, one numbered payload every 10 ms
traffic.transport: TCP with TCP_NODELAY enabled; TCP-reconnect reconnects once every 10 ms until connected

blocking.global_schedule: form a multiset of exactly 220 trials for each of the six mechanism-arm pairs, for exactly 1320 trials total; deterministically shuffle that multiset with the fixed seed; partition the shuffled sequence into 66 consecutive host-epoch blocks of exactly 20 total trials
blocking.warmup_assignment: for each mechanism-arm pair, its first 20 occurrences in the shuffled sequence are warmups and its remaining 200 occurrences are measured trials
blocking.randomization: the deterministic global shuffle is the sole trial order; no within-block re-randomization occurs

timing_and_actions.candidate_proof_timeout: 3 seconds, matching frozen challenge expiry; it never extends the T+5-second observation window
timing_and_actions.worker_supervisor: may allow up to 40 seconds solely for bounded teardown and error capture, never for measurement; it may probe static source-policy routes with `ip route get` without emitting output or traffic

abrupt-break.R8: old and candidate carriers use the fixed server addresses and UDP port 53104; one process and session retain state. At T, bring the candidate interface up and administratively bring the old interface down before one authenticated LOC_UPDATE and the sole candidate probe/challenge/response proof; no fallback is permitted.
abrupt-break.TCP-reconnect: Old and new listeners are explicitly SO_BINDTODEVICE-bound to their corresponding server interfaces and their numeric address and port; no wildcard or weak-host listener is permitted. The established stream initially uses numeric 10.88.1.2:53101. At T, make the new listener and interface usable, administratively bring the old server interface down, and reconnect every 10 ms without DNS to the preconfigured numeric target 10.88.1.3:53102.
abrupt-break.GARP-VIP: the stream initially connects to 10.88.1.100:53103 on the old interface. At T, make the new interface usable and atomically remove then add the VIP; as part of that atomic move, execute exactly one `ip route replace table 103 10.88.0.0/24 via 10.88.1.1 dev candidate onlink`, then execute exactly three `arping -U -c 1 -w 1` commands, each sending one unsolicited announcement. Operations start 100 ms apart and each bounded command MUST return before the next; return 0 or 1 is successful evidence because no reply is expected, and any other return fails. The listener is wildcard-bound within the isolated server namespace; no neighbor flush is permitted. No R8 or TCP route changes occur at cutover.

make-before-break.activation: at T-2 seconds activate the new carrier, listener/interface, or VIP interface respectively; do not cut over traffic
make-before-break.R8: old and candidate carriers use the fixed server addresses and UDP port 53104; one process and session retain state. Bring the candidate interface up at T-2 seconds; at or after T perform one authenticated LOC_UPDATE and the sole candidate proof, retain the old carrier until proof, then make it grace-only and administratively down after grace. No fallback is permitted.
make-before-break.TCP-reconnect: Old and new listeners are explicitly SO_BINDTODEVICE-bound to their corresponding server interfaces and their numeric address and port; no wildcard or weak-host listener is permitted. The established stream initially uses numeric 10.88.1.2:53101. At T-2 seconds make the new listener and interface usable; at T administratively bring the old server interface down and reconnect every 10 ms without DNS to numeric 10.88.1.3:53102.
make-before-break.GARP-VIP: the stream initially connects to 10.88.1.100:53103 on the old interface. Bring the new interface up at T-2 seconds; at T atomically remove then add the VIP and, as part of that atomic move, execute exactly one `ip route replace table 103 10.88.0.0/24 via 10.88.1.1 dev candidate onlink`, then execute exactly three `arping -U -c 1 -w 1` commands, each sending one unsolicited announcement. Operations start 100 ms apart and each bounded command MUST return before the next; return 0 or 1 is successful evidence because no reply is expected, and any other return fails. The listener is wildcard-bound within the isolated server namespace; no neighbor flush is permitted. No R8 or TCP route changes occur at cutover.

equalization.trust: all peers use preconfigured closed-lab trust before the trial; no PKI, TOFU, or trust change during a trial
equalization.candidate_mechanism: R8 uses only the contract mechanism in spec/0006-mobility-v0.1.md; no dynamic routing, fallback, passive promotion, or alternate candidate mechanism

readiness_and_outage.readiness: first 10 consecutive on-schedule post-T payload deliveries
readiness_and_outage.outage_start: last successfully received pre-T sequence-numbered payload
readiness_and_outage.timeout: a trial without readiness by T+5 seconds is censored at T+5 seconds and retained as failure

collection.interface_counters: record pre-trial and T+5-second per-interface rx_bytes, tx_bytes, rx_packets, tx_packets, rx_dropped, tx_dropped, rx_errors, and tx_errors; output identifies interfaces only by ordinal and count
collection.process_cpu: record process user_cpu_ns and system_cpu_ns over T-3 seconds through T+5 seconds
collection.identifier_redaction: results and telemetry record configuration_sha256 only and MUST NOT record raw IP address, port, argv, LOC, namespace name, interface name, veth name, VIP, route, or command.
collection.endpoint_failure_classification: An endpoint process failure after T-3 seconds is an outcome failure with setup_status=complete; retain available authenticated events and counters and never make it a setup exclusion. Only launch or readiness failures before schedule are setup failures.

error_category.child_error_mapping: Only an exact redacted child token maps to an outcome category; stderr and argv MUST NOT be emitted.

exclusions.only: setup failure retained as a raw row with setup_status=failed and exclusion_reason=setup_failure
exclusions.forbidden: no other exclusion, retry, replacement, omission, or post-hoc filtering

block_bootstrap_95_percent_ci.value_form: each field is [2.5th percentile, 97.5th percentile] over bootstrap resamples, or null when its estimator has no defined resamples
block_bootstrap_95_percent_ci.sampling: deterministically resample the 66 complete 20-trial blocks with replacement
block_bootstrap_95_percent_ci.per_pair_rows: for each mechanism-arm pair and each resample, include all selected measured pair rows occurring in sampled blocks; blocks with zero rows for that pair are valid and no block is required to contain the pair
block_bootstrap_95_percent_ci.failure_rate: compute over all resampled pair rows
block_bootstrap_95_percent_ci.outage_quantiles: compute only over nonfailed uncensored outage values among the resampled pair rows
